title: Trade signal
description: What the agent service answers when the engine asks about one instrument. The agents give a view; they never give an amount. Sizing is the engine's job, which is what keeps a prompt injection from becoming a large order. See decision 1 in docs/arkitektur-roadmap.md.

stance.description: The direction the agents argue for. The engine decides whether anything is actually traded.

conviction.description: How strongly the agents hold the view. It is not calibrated, so the engine maps it to discrete tiers rather than scaling an amount by it.

thesis.description: Why, in the agents' own words. Stored, never parsed. Capped because an uncapped free-text field is one an agent can fill with anything, and every reader downstream pays for it: the next step's prompt, the engine, stage 4's decision table.

key_risks.description: What would make the thesis wrong. Capped for the same reason as the thesis.

horizon_days.description: The period the view is meant to play out over. Stage 4 measures the outcome at this horizon and at fixed ones, so that two team versions can be compared.

reference_price.description: The quote the view was formed on. The engine sizes the order from this, so the agent service returns it rather than the engine fetching market data of its own.

quote_as_of.description: When that quote was taken. The engine refuses a signal formed on a stale quote.

instrument.description: A discriminated union on 'type'. Only equity exists today; a derivative becomes a new variant rather than a breaking change. The engine refuses a type it does not know.

symbol.description: Uppercase, as the engine's Ticker normalises it.

run.description: How the answer was produced. The engine does not decide on any of it, but it stores it, so that stage 4 can compare outcomes per team setup.

team_version.description: A hash of the team's specification and its prompt files. A changed prompt is a new version, or two different teams end up in the same statistics.

revisions.description: How many review rounds the run took. Always 0 until review rounds exist; the field is here from the start, because adding one later would be a contract change.

existing_position.description: What the portfolio already holds of this instrument, or null. The engine knows this; it is sent so that the agents stop proposing amounts the risk rules will reject.

request.description: What the engine asks. It carries the limits, so that the agents reason inside them rather than against them.

team_id.description: Which team setup to run. The engine sends 'default' until stage 3 makes teams selectable.

available_risk_budget_usd.description: What the engine is willing to spend on this instrument right now, after its own rules.

max_position_pct.description: The largest share of net asset value one position may take.

correlation_id.description: One analysis, one id. Both services store it in a varchar(64), which is what the cap is.
